image_description: A low-angle, medium-shot photograph of a massive white radio telescope (resembling the Lovell Telescope at Jodrell Bank). The image features a colossal parabolic dish antenna constructed from a metal mesh surface supported by an intricate white steel lattice truss structure. The dish is mounted on a large, complex alt-azimuth support tower with visible mechanical gearing and walkways. In the foreground, there are green bushes and grass; in the background, trees and a cloudy sky. The scale is emphasized by the dwarfing of the surrounding vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous parabolic dish antenna of colossal scale, dwarfing all surrounding structures.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish dominates the frame and clearly dwarfs the trees and bushes in the foreground, confirming colossal scale.
The rim of the dish forms a consistent elliptical projection indicative of a precise parabolic curve viewed from an angle. No warping or irregularity is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the object is large, the 'visible from great distances' attribute requires a long-range perspective shot which is not provided in this close-up/medium shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Receiver feed horn at focal point of dish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A complex sub-reflector and feed horn assembly is clearly suspended on struts at the geometric focal point of the dish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish rests on a massive, multi-legged steel tower structure with visible pivot points, characteristic of an alt-azimuth mount.
The base of the support tower shows a circular track foundation and heavy machinery housing, implying rotational capability.
The support legs anchor into a substantial ground-level structure that appears to be reinforced concrete/steel, partially obscured by bushes but structurally evident.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal mesh or solid aluminum panel dish surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface of the dish exhibits a fine grid pattern consistent with metal mesh construction, allowing visibility through the surface in some areas.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Astronomical instrument for detecting radio-frequency emissions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall configuration (dish + feed + mount) is uniquely identifiable as a radio telescope.
The heavy-duty mechanical joints and counterweight-like structures on the mount are consistent with mechanisms required for tracking celestial bodies.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and distinguish it from similar structures like satellite dishes or solar concentrators.
To verify the structural integrity of the complex lattice truss work and ensure the parabolic depth is physically consistent without melting or spatial bleeding.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the thin white steel beams and the sky/background, a common AI artifact in complex linear structures.
To assess general texture consistency of the metal mesh and detect any subtle noise or blur artifacts.

focus_areas: Integrity of the lattice truss structure (no broken or fused beams)
Consistency of the parabolic curve geometry
Sharpness of boundaries between the white structure and the sky
Texture realism of the metal mesh surface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the intersection points of the steel lattice. AI generators often struggle with the connectivity of complex truss systems, leading to floating beams or impossible joints. Verify if the feed horn suspension struts connect logically to the dish rim and the central hub. Check for any 'haloing' or soft edges around the high-contrast white beams against the grey sky.
